standard.title: Joined handwriting fluency
standard.description: write words using clearly formed joined letters, with developing fluency and automaticity
standard.prior_knowledge: Students form letters with developing consistency (prior year handwriting). They have not yet developed fluency and automaticity with clearly formed joined letters.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can write words using clearly formed joined letters with developing fluency and automaticity, so that handwriting does not impede composition.

nodes.label: Clearly formed joined letters
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can write words using correctly formed joined letters that are legible to a reader.
nodes.minimum_width: Write a short piece of text using joined letters that are legible and consistently formed.
nodes.typical_width: Write extended pieces using joined letters across a range of tasks, maintaining legibility and consistent letter formation throughout.
wider: Limited width — joined handwriting fluency is a motor skill that does not vary meaningfully across contexts at this year band. Extension involves writing at greater length and speed while maintaining legibility, not broadening application across contexts.
nodes.hinge_reason: Developing fluency and automaticity in N2 requires correctly formed letters — practising at speed with incorrect formation reinforces the wrong habits and is harder to remediate later.

response_modes.reason: Handwriting automaticity is built through practice volume. Fluency and automaticity with joined letters require sustained practice — there is no conceptual breadth to exploit, only time on task.

success_criteria: Joined letters are legible — a reader can identify all letters without assistance
Letter formation is consistent across a piece of writing

nodes.label: Developing fluency and automaticity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can write with developing speed and fluency so that handwriting does not slow down or interrupt the composition process.
nodes.minimum_width: Write a short piece at a pace that does not significantly interrupt the flow of ideas — composition is not held up by letter formation.
nodes.typical_width: Write extended texts with developing automaticity — letter formation is sufficiently fluent that students can focus cognitive attention on composing rather than forming letters.
wider: Limited width — handwriting automaticity is a motor fluency target, not a conceptual one. The enrichment direction is sustained practice with increasing text length.

response_modes.reason: Automaticity is achieved through practice volume, not conceptual breadth. Students need extended writing practice to develop the fluency this descriptor targets.

success_criteria: Can complete a sustained writing task without stopping to think about letter formation
Writing pace is sufficient for the task demand
